what_this_adds: A fourth matched control pair for VLM geometry judging: an occlusion defect, which controls-v3 does not contain and whose schema cannot express it.

A1_one_camera_one_geometry.how: Both frames share the fitted camera and the same three layer PLYs; only the retained-surface layer differs.

A2_defect_visible_in_pixels_below_50_per.required: subject footprint in D4_occluded below 50% of D4_unoccluded
A2_defect_visible_in_pixels_below_50_per.not_moved: The threshold stands as frozen. It was chosen to match #1014's geometric gate so the two instruments would answer on one boundary, and that was a mistake made before measuring: the ray cast's denominator is total surface area including back faces, the rasterizer's is screen footprint. The same defect is 35.2% visible by area and 52.2% by footprint, because the hidden regions are at grazing angles -- much area, few pixels. Recording the failure rather than relabelling the quantity.
A2_defect_visible_in_pixels_below_50_per.what_did_hold: The defect is unmistakable in the delivered frames by a measurement I did not freeze: 51,864 pixels differ, and the retained surface accounts for 46,562 pale pixels in D4_occluded against 11,463 in D4_unoccluded.

A3_prediction_at_least_2_of_4_accept_the.result: confirmed, and more strongly than predicted

acceptance_as_frozen.A4_not_a_qualification: No judge is qualified or disqualified. v3's negative result stands. #1014 remains vlm_eval not_applicable; nothing here is a visual acceptance gate for it.

the_finding: All four judges accepted the occluded frame as adequate for reviewing the surface it hides. This is v3's clipped-frame result in a fourth defect class: there, every parsed call called a reproducibly clipped frame reviewable and accepted it. The mechanism is not a perception failure -- seeing an occluder and judging the subject behind it unreadable are different steps, and these judges do not take the second one. Only Kimi K3 called the subject partly hidden, and it accepted the frame anyway.

confusion.note: Every false accept is on D4_occluded; every D4_unoccluded verdict is right.

probe_limitation: Kimi K2.6 and GLM 5.3 Flash returned byte-identical values on all three fields across two frames differing by 51,864 pixels, so their calls carry no evidence of image sensitivity and their false accepts are correspondingly weaker evidence, not interchangeable with the other two.
limits: Two frames, one scene, four hosted models, one call each. Not judge qualification, not geometry accuracy, not generalization, and not a visual gate for any PR.
how_many_judges_the_mechanism_claim_rest: Two, not four. This first said all four 'correctly reported the pale occluding surface as present, so they saw it', which does not survive the probe limitation recorded beside it: two of the four returned byte-identical answers for two different images, so nothing in their calls shows they saw anything. Review raised the contradiction between the two statements. The accept count is four; the evidenced mechanism is two.
the_probe_premise_this_corrects: The probe was first written on pale_surface_present alone: the frames differ in pale coverage, so a model reading pixels had to answer that field differently. A reviewer disproved the inference with a call rather than an argument -- a fifth model varied subject_visibility across the pair, so it read both images, and still answered pale identically. The field asks whether a large smooth pale surface is present, not whether there is more of one, and 11,463 pale pixels is a visible patch, so yes is defensible for both frames and the expected no was a threshold judgement dressed as a ground truth. The discriminator above does not depend on any single field being right: byte-identical everywhere is no evidence, varying anything is evidence. It separates the same two groups.
where_the_discriminator_is_weakest: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash varies exactly one field, and it is pale_surface_present -- the field whose reliability the correction above questions. Its answer moved in the defensible direction (yes on the occluded frame, no on the unoccluded one), which is real evidence it tracked the pixels, but it is one field. Kimi K3 varies two, including subject_visibility, and is the only judge whose evidence of reading does not rest on the contested field. Review's note says DeepSeek varied two; it varied one. Recorded because it changes how much weight each of the two judges carries, not whether the grouping holds.
frozen_plan_retention: frozen_plan_sha256 is the sha256 of the frozen criteria document for this claim, which is retained in the program's private claim directory and is deliberately not committed -- that directory is program coordination state and is not part of the repository. It names no file in Git by design. The hash still verifies against the retained document, and the criteria it covers (A1 through A5, including the A2 threshold this run failed) are reproduced verbatim under acceptance_as_frozen below, so a reader can see what was frozen without access to the directory.

pale_coverage_measured.why: Review reports 9.96% of the occluded frame and 4.74% of the unoccluded one. I could not reproduce those under any definition I tried, so both measurements are recorded with their definitions rather than one being asserted over the other. The disagreement does not affect the premise correction above, which is a logic error either way.
pale_coverage_measured.which_one_the_harness_quoted: The harness's 46,562 and 11,463 reproduce the loosest definition above to within 0.4%, so those figures are sound. Under every definition the occluded frame carries 4x to 60x more pale coverage than the unoccluded one, against the roughly 2x in review's figures.
